papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) remains an aggressive malignancy with limited durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and no established predictive biomarkers. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and predictive value of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in patients with ES-SCLC receiving ICI-based therapy. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of 180 treatment-naïve ES-SCLC patients subsequently receiving ICI-based therapy, TLSs were systematically evaluated using H&E staining, multiplex immunofluorescence, and spatial analysis to determine their prognostic and predictive value. RESULTS: TLSs were identified in 22.2% of cases and independently associated with improved overall survival (OS) in both univariate (HR = 0.365, 95% CI: 0.217-0.613, P < 0.001) and multivariate (HR = 0.337, 95% CI: 0.199-0.569, P < 0.001) analyses. Crucially, TLS maturation status was associated with clinical outcomes, as patients with mature TLSs containing CD21+ follicular dendritic cells and organized germinal centers experienced significantly longer survival than those with non-mature TLSs (P = 0.0049). Beyond mere presence, responders to ICIs exhibited distinct spatial characteristics, including higher TLS densities, denser immune infiltration, and shorter distances between TLS-resident CD20+ B cells, CD3+ T cells, and tumor cells, suggesting that immune-tumor spatial organization within TLSs reflects functional antitumor engagement. CONCLUSION: TLS maturation and spatial architecture may serve as candidate tissue biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes in ICI-treated ES-SCLC, warranting prospective validation alongside SCLC molecular subtyping.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundRural esophageal cancer patients experience both fragmented and delayed care. One-size-fits-all interventions aimed at rural communities can be ineffective, as they can vary significantly in population, geographic isolation, and medical specialty availability. Therefore, as a rural health care center, we analyzed the journey of care for our esophageal cancer patients to better understand and serve our community. We aimed to create a framework for how to approach and analyze this complex care continuum for other small communities.MethodsEsophageal cancer patients receiving care at a rural cancer center from September 2024 to April 2025 were enrolled. Care journeys were mapped from symptom onset through treatment. Interviews occurred at enrollment and 3 months.ResultsTwenty-seven patients were enrolled. Nearly half (48%) presented with metastatic disease. Patients on average reported symptoms 85 days after onset, were diagnosed 137 days after onset, and started treatment 48 day after diagnosis. Metastatic patients experienced shorter times to treatment (72 vs 128 days, P = 0.014) compared to locoregional patients. Surgical patients averaged 57 days from diagnosis to starting neoadjuvant treatment, followed by 97 days from completing neoadjuvant treatment to esophagectomy. Patients reported disempowerment, difficulty navigating the medical system, and a lack of awareness before diagnosis.ConclusionsRural esophageal cancer patients endure prolonged, fragmented, and variable care journeys. Surgical patients, in particular, face delays before esophagectomy. Rural research provides valuable insights for tailoring broader interventions for rural communities. In partnership, rural centers and universities provide both bottom-up and top-down perspectives in defragmenting rural esophageal cancer care.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is a rare and aggressive cancer with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Unlike other thoracic cancers responding well to immunotherapy, PM typically lacks key predictive biomarkers such as Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor expression. Nonetheless, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have shown clinical activity in PM, particularly in non-epithelioid subtypes. However, only a subset of patients benefits from this approach, and resistance remains a major challenge. A growing body of evidence suggests that tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a central role in shaping this resistance. In PM, the TME is notably immunosuppressive, dominated by regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and tumor-associated macrophages. These elements act as a shield against immune activation, limiting the efficacy of ICIs. Novel therapeutic strategies aimed at depleting or modulating suppressive immune populations within the TME are emerging as promising avenues to overcome resistance and enhance the effectiveness of ICIs. In this narrative review, we examine the unique features of the TME in PM, its role in immunotherapy resistance, and emerging strategies aimed at harnessing or remodeling the TME to improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitor response in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) reflects coordinated tumor and immune states that are not fully captured by single biomarkers. We developed scTIME, an interpretable model that translates single-cell immune programs into bulk transcriptomic scores, and integrated public single-cell, T-cell receptor, transcriptomic, survival, and proteogenomic cohorts. Response modeling used two cohorts with different endpoints (40 patients) and compared six algorithms. ElasticNet was selected as a sparse reporting model, achieving a pooled five-fold out-of-fold ROC-AUC of 0.810; nested model selection yielded 0.772. Matched held-out stratification identified response-enriched scTIME groups in a direct descriptive comparison with CD274, while the fitted score emphasized cytotoxic CD8, natural killer, SPP1 macrophage, interferon-response, and antigen-presentation programs. Single-cell analyses and external projections linked these programs to CXCL10-CXCR3 recruitment, exclusion-associated states, and T-cell receptor ecology across molecular contexts. Exploratory survival and cross-omics analyses extended the framework beyond the response cohorts but were interpreted as projection rather than independent validation. Together, the results show how cell-resolved immune biology can support transparent, multi-omic biomarker development without reducing response to a single pathway. scTIME remains exploratory because model choice was post hoc, cohorts were small and clinically heterogeneous, and endpoint-matched external validation was unavailable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is a major iatrogenic complication of mechanical ventilation, in which dysregulated inflammation, particularly macrophage-driven response, amplifies pulmonary damage. Although bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling exhibits context-dependent effects in pulmonary disorders, whether specific BMP receptors (BMPRs) regulate macrophage function during VILI remains unknown. METHODS: Mice subjected to mechanical ventilation were randomly divided into Control (intubation without ventilation), LVT (low tidal volume), and HVT (high tidal volume) groups. HVT-exposed mice received intratracheal administration of exogenous BMP4 or the BMP type I receptor antagonist LDN193189. Lung injury severity was assessed by ultrasound, macroscopic scoring, wet/dry ratio, and histopathology. Macrophage accumulation, M1/M2 polarization, interstitial-to-alveolar macrophage (IM/AM) ratio, and BMP receptor expression were evaluated. Transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. In vitro, gain- and loss-of-function experiments (overexpression and knockdown of BMPRIB) were conducted in RAW264.7 macrophages to assess cytokine/chemokine production, migration, and MAPK pathway activation. The p38 inhibitor SB202190 was used to probe downstream signaling. RESULTS: Compared with Control and LVT groups, HVT induced time-dependent macrophage accumulation, skewed M1/M2 polarization, and a progressive elevation of the IM/AM ratio. Strikingly, HVT selectively upregulated BMPRIB in lung macrophages, while downregulating BMPRII and leaving BMPRIA unchanged. Intratracheal BMP4 exacerbated these effects, whereas LDN193189 reversed BMP4-induced macrophage accumulation, M1 polarization, IM/AM elevation, and suppressed activation of ERK, JNK, p38, and p65 signaling. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that BMP4 enriched MAPK and inflammation-related pathways, with LDN193189 co-treatment partially reversing this enrichment. In BMP4-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, BMPRIB overexpression enhanced, whereas BMPRIB knockdown attenuated, cytokine/chemokine production and migration. Pharmacological p38 inhibition (SB202190) abrogated BMP4-induced pro-inflammatory effects in macrophages. CONCLUSIONS: HVT-induced BMPRIB upregulation in lung macrophages allows BMP4 to activate BMPRIB-dependent p38/NF-κB p65 axis as a key mediator of macrophage-driven inflammation in VILI Targeting the BMPRIB-dependent p38/NF-κB axis may represent a novel therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Subsolid pulmonary nodules (SSNs), including pure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) and part-solid nodules (PSNs), span transient inflammatory abnormalities and adenocarcinoma-spectrum lesions with widely different management implications. This critical narrative review treats CT reconstruction as part of the quantitative biomarker definition and asks whether targeted or high-spatial-resolution reconstruction provides stable, task-specific information beyond standardized thin-section CT. Evidence was synthesized across direct SSN reconstruction-domain studies, technical robustness studies, and clinical prediction studies. Direct imaging studies support improved depiction of selected fine structures, while same-scan GGN evidence demonstrates substantial pixel-size dependence of radiomic features and model composition. However, most clinical models were not evaluated in paired reconstruction domains, external validation with calibration remains uncommon, and no prospective study demonstrating management or patient benefit from reconstruction-aware radiomics in SSNs was identified in the literature reviewed. Persistent pGGNs provide a biological and technical rationale for investigating incremental quantitative information, but greater benefit than in PSNs has not been demonstrated. In PSNs, any model must add value beyond solid-component measurements, consolidation-to-tumor ratio, morphology, and longitudinal growth. Translation therefore requires reconstruction and segmentation robustness testing, strong conventional comparators, external calibration, prespecified thresholds, and prospective decision-linked evaluation. Until such benefit and safety are demonstrated, reconstruction-aware radiomics should remain investigational or confined to governed, domain-checked decision-support pathways.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Osimertinib and cisplatin are widely used as standard treatments for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, their effects on tumor microenvironment remodeling remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether TREM2-positive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) promote immune evasion through the CCL5/CCL22-CCR5/CCR4-Treg axis under anticancer treatment. METHODS: The spatial and quantitative correlations between TREM2+ and FOXP3+ cells were assessed using NSCLC patient-derived single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets, human lung adenocarcinoma tissue microarrays, and cisplatin-treated mouse lung cancer models. RESULTS: scRNA-seq dataset analysis showed significantly enriched TREM2+ and FOXP3+ cells in lung adenocarcinoma tissues compared with adjacent normal lung, with a significant positive correlation at the aggregated single-cell level (Spearman's rho = 0.7323, P < 0.001). CCL5 and CCL22 were identified as key mediators linking TREM2+ TAMs and FOXP3+ Tregs and were markedly induced by treatment but suppressed by TREM2 knockdown or pharmacologic inhibition. TREM2 overexpression further enhanced their induction. Mechanistically, CCL22 induction was broadly dependent on SYK, Src, AKT, NF-κB, or STAT3 signaling pathways, whereas CCL5 upregulation depended on Src, NF-κB, and STAT3, with SYK involvement varying by cell type. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that TREM2+ TAMs drive CCL5/CCL22-mediated Treg recruitment and support targeting TREM2 to enhance therapeutic efficacy of standard NSCLC treatments.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a major public health priority, with survival shaped by clinical, behavioral, socioeconomic, and organizational factors. Socioeconomic disadvantage may affect risk exposure, diagnosis, treatment access, continuity of care, and data completeness. OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between area-level socioeconomic deprivation and cause-specific survival in lung cancer and apply the M.A.S.T.E.R. (Methodological Approach for Strategic Transformation, Evaluation, and Redesign) framework to translate epidemiological evidence into organizational design and implementation planning. METHODS: A retrospective population-based registry cohort study within ASL Napoli 1 Centro included incident malignant tumors of the trachea, lung, and bronchi recorded between 2010 and 2023. Cancer Registry data were integrated with the 2021 Socioeconomic Disadvantage Index (IDISE), Hospital Discharge Records, and progressi delle Aziende Sanitarie per la Salute in Italia (PASSI) 2022-2024 contextual smoking prevalence by sex and Primary Health Care District (DSB). Cause-specific survival was analyzed using multivariable Cox regression with district-clustered robust variance; Fine-Gray competing-risk regression was used as sensitivity analysis. M.A.S.T.E.R. comprised six phases: Mapping and contextualization, analysis and diagnosis, strategic design, testing and adaptive execution, embedding and sustainability, and resilience and renewal. RESULTS: Of 11,162 cases, 10,039 were included in the main analysis, totaling 207,600 person-months. There were 8,514 deaths, including 6,990 cause-specific deaths. In the primary model without contextual smoking prevalence, adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) increased across deprivation quintiles (Q5 vs. Q1: HR 1.11; 95% CI: 1.05-1.18; p < 0.001). Adding PASSI smoking prevalence attenuated the estimates (Q5 vs. Q1: HR 1.09; 95% CI: 0.99-1.19; p = 0.069); smoking prevalence was not statistically associated with mortality. M.A.S.T.E.R. outputs included a qualitative failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), a plan, do, study, act (PDSA) protocol with control plan, a completeness dashboard, and plans for updates, audits, and strategic review. CONCLUSIONS: Greater area-level socioeconomic deprivation was associated with higher cause-specific mortality in the primary model; the association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adding contextual PASSI smoking prevalence. M.A.S.T.E.R. clarified the transition from epidemiological analysis to candidate interventions for prevention, smoking cessation, early diagnosis, patient navigation, and information integration. Outputs from the final four phases are design-oriented and require prospective implementation and validation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To examine whether Medicare's 2018 National Coverage Determination (NCD) for next-generation sequencing (NGS) was associated with changes in the use of targeted oral anticancer therapies among older adults with lung cancer. METHODS: Retrospective cohort study. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate the probability of initiating an oral targeted therapy within 12 months of diagnosis. papers.abstract_en: The clinical translation of RNA interference (RNAi) for lung cancer treatment remains hampered by the lack of delivery vectors that concurrently optimize cellular uptake, target specificity, and in vivo stability. This work reports an intrinsically chiral gold nanoparticle (Au NP) platform with precisely controlled morphology for targeted siRNA delivery. Through a full 2 × 2 factorial design (2 chiralities × 2 morphologies), the work decouples the individual and combined contributions of these two parameters. It is found that right-handed chiral nanoparticles (D-NPs) show significantly faster cellular internalization and higher gene silencing potency than left-handed (L-NPs) and achiral (DL-NPs) counterparts. Beyond chirality, nanoparticle morphology serves as an equally critical parameter: the rhombicuboctahedral (RCO) architecture yields markedly higher silencing efficacy than cubic counterparts with D-chirality. Furthermore, proteomic analysis revealed that Au RCO nanoparticles with different chirality displayed distinct functional enrichment profiles. By D-RCO combination with minimal surface modification, siRNA targeting PD-L1 achieves potent knockdown and robust inhibition of H460 lung cancer proliferation both in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes chirality and morphology as co-designable parameters for gene delivery and provides a mechanistic blueprint for translating chiral nanomaterials into solid tumor therapy.

Key findings include: epithelial cells in severe lung cancer exhibit significantly attenuated inflammation- and immunity-related signaling pathways (including NF-κB, TNF, and JAK-STAT signaling pathways), enhanced stem cell-like properties, and metabolic reprogramming; we identified a highly stem-like malignant epithelial cell subpopulation, represented by Cluster 3, which is enriched in stem-like pathways such as Notch, Hippo, TGF-β, and FoxO, and is accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial metabolism and stress adaptability; STMN1 is a key molecule regulating this stem-like state, showing a significant positive correlation with stemness scores and mRNAi; cells with high STMN1 expression gain a survival advantage and may maintain their stemness by attenuating CAF/ECM signaling with other cells (COL1A1-CD44), inhibiting complement activation and antigen presentation signaling (such as C3, ANXA1, and MHC-II-related molecules), and enhancing stemness niche signaling (MIF-CD74/CD44). Furthermore, NELFE, MYBL2, FOXN3, POLR2A, and RAD21 were identified as potential upstream regulators of STMN1. In vitro experiments confirmed that, following induction of stem cell-like properties, STMN1 was significantly overexpressed in lung adenocarcinoma cells, accompanied by upregulation of related stem cell markers (SOX2, NANOG, OCT4, and CD44). In summary, this study reveals a significantly enhanced stemness state in malignant epithelial cells in advanced lung cancer, accompanied by suppressed inflammatory signaling and enhanced metabolic adaptation, and identifies STMN1 as a key molecule driving stemness maintenance and disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: Ras-related protein Rab7a participates in fundamental cancer cell processes; however, its role in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to define Rab7a's oncogenic functions in ESCC and its involvement in the Hippo signaling pathway. Rab7a expression was assessed using ESCC datasets and validated by immunohistochemical analysis of ESCC tissues. We examined functional effects using small interfering RNA knockdown and Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) overexpression rescue experiments, primarily by evaluating proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis in ESCC TE-1 cells. We also established a xenograft model for in vivo validation. Regarding its mechanism(s) of action, we analyzed the effects of Rab7a on Hippo core kinases (LATS1/2 and MOB1) and further assessed YAP nuclear localization in ESCC cells. Rab7a was overexpressed in ESCC tissues, and elevated expression correlated with aggressive clinicopathological features, including advanced tumor, node, metastasis stage, positive lymph node metastasis, deep tumor invasion, and poor differentiation. Rab7a knockdown suppressed cellular proliferation, migration, and invasion and induced apoptosis in vitro while inhibiting tumor growth and decreasing Ki-67 expression in vivo. Mechanistically, Rab7a silencing downregulated YAP1, p-YAP1, CTGF, and survivin without affecting MST1. Furthermore, Rab7a knockdown significantly increased p-LATS1/2 levels without altering total LATS1/2 or MOB1 expression and decreased YAP nuclear accumulation. To address this, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model that mechanistically recapitulates signaling networks and drug responses across all three classes, integrating multiscale preclinical-to-clinical datasets. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific mortality in high-risk populations, yet screening rates remain low nationwide. papers.abstract_en: The intratumor microbiome, one of the hallmarks of cancer, plays a crucial role in cancer progression through its interaction with the host. However, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, six publicly available single-cell transcriptomic lung cancer datasets (comprising 178 samples) from multiple centers (Shanghai, New York, Seoul) were integrated to investigate the heterogeneity of host-microbiome interactions at the single-cell level using single-cell analysis of host-microbiome interactions (SAHMI). Finally, specific cell-associated bacteria are significantly correlated with clinical features, such as lung cancer stages and smoking frequency. These single-cell insights into microbiome-host interactions improve current understanding about lung cancer development and progression and offer potential micro-ecological and diagnostic insights.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset (n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are distinctive toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and have been reported to correlate with clinical outcomes in several cancers. However, whether this association also exists in patients with esophageal cancer (EC) receiving ICIs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the association between irAEs and clinical outcomes in this population. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated the association between irAEs and progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), or disease control rate (DCR). Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled for PFS and OS, whereas odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were pooled for ORR and DCR using random-effects models. Between-study heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals (PIs), sensitivity analyses, publication bias, prespecified subgroup analyses, and immortal-time bias were also assessed. RESULTS: 14 studies involving 1, 546 patients were included. The occurrence of irAEs was associated with improved PFS (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.31-0.63), OS (HR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.46-0.64), ORR (OR, 4.00; 95% CI, 1.58-10.12), and DCR (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 2.40-6.20). The 95% PIs were 0.16-1.24, 0.44-0.66, 0.19-82.57, and 1.42-10.44 for PFS, OS, ORR, and DCR, respectively, crossing the null value for PFS and ORR. Subgroup estimates were generally similar in direction but remained exploratory. No eligible survival estimates using landmark or time-varying approaches were available for the comparison between patients with and without irAEs. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with EC receiving ICIs, the occurrence of irAEs may be a prognostic marker of favorable outcomes. However, wide PIs for PFS and ORR indicate that these associations may vary across future studies and immortal time bias may overestimate survival associations. This observational evidence derives mainly from East Asian patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and is primarily applicable to these patients. Subgroup findings remain exploratory and require prospective validation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261346294.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Although pleural tissue debris is occasionally encountered in the drainage systems of patients undergoing catheter or chest tube drainage, its clinical utility has not been reported. Here, we report two cases in which pleural tissue debris retrieved during catheter drainage enabled a definitive diagnosis of malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and molecularly guided treatment decisions. CASE PRESENTATION: The first case involved a 67-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease who developed a right pleural effusion suggestive of lung cancer with pleural metastasis. Invasive procedures for tissue acquisition were required; however, biopsy was withheld because of the high risk of pneumothorax and acute exacerbation of the underlying lung disease. Tissue debris was incidentally found in the drainage system. The tissue was adequate for pathological examination and revealed lung squamous cell carcinoma without genomic alterations. Chemoimmunotherapy was initiated without further invasive procedures. The second case involved a 78-year-old woman who presented with a left pleural effusion and a brain lesion, highly suggestive of lung cancer with brain metastasis. She declined invasive diagnostic procedures; however, tissue debris was incidentally collected from the drainage bottle and diagnosed as lung adenocarcinoma. Molecular testing revealed that the tumor harbored an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R mutation, allowing first-line targeted therapy to be initiated without further invasive testing. CONCLUSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first case report to describe the clinical utility of pleural tissue debris for the diagnosis of MPE and its suitability for molecular profiling. Our report highlights that this previously overlooked byproduct of routine pleural drainage can provide adequate material for histopathological diagnosis, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing in patients with MPE, particularly those for whom conventional biopsy is contraindicated or declined.

papers.abstract_en: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is an ultra-rare vascular neoplasm with variable biologic behavior. Mediastinal EHE is particularly uncommon and may mimic more prevalent prevascular mediastinal tumors. We report a 52-year-old man with a 10.5 × 8.9 × 9.6 cm mixed-density left upper anterior mediastinal mass containing macroscopic fat, soft-tissue components, and coarse calcification. FDG PET/CT demonstrated mild-to-moderate uptake (SUVmax 4.8) without nodal or distant metastatic disease, and the imaging appearance favored mature teratoma. Resection demonstrated a 9.5 cm conventional EHE intimately associated with a myelolipomatous component containing extensive extramedullary hematopoiesis and metaplastic ossification. The neoplastic cells expressed endothelial markers, and RNA fusion analysis detected WWTR1::CAMTA1. Surgical margins were negative, early postoperative and abdominopelvic imaging showed no residual or metastatic disease, and multidisciplinary review recommended surveillance without adjuvant therapy. Although similar EHE-myelolipoma/extramedullary hematopoiesis associations have been reported, this case emphasizes the multimodality imaging mimic of mature teratoma and provides direct radiologic-pathologic correlation of the fat-containing, solid, and ossified components.

papers.abstract_en: Gastric and esophageal cancers pose major global health challenges due to high incidence, frequent late-stage diagnosis, and poor survival outcomes. This review synthesized current evidence on emerging technologies and innovative approaches shaping research and practice. We included studies that evaluated diagnostic imaging, endoscopic and surgical treatments, molecular biomarkers, staging, screening, and innovative therapeutic approaches in gastric and esophageal cancers. The review revealed notable demographic and geographic disparities in disease incidence and outcomes. Recent advancements in endoscopic techniques, imaging modalities, and staging systems have enhanced early detection and prognostic stratification. Intriguing findings include significant improvements in survival with HER2-targeted and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies, the ability of liquid biopsy to detect resistance mutations and monitor treatment efficacy in real time, and the use of patient-derived organoids to predict individualized responses. Additionally, artificial intelligence (AI) applications have reduced diagnostic variability, thereby refining therapeutic decision-making. Despite promising innovations, further validation of these emerging technologies is required. Integrating advanced imaging, biomarker-based treatments, and AI-driven tools into clinical practice holds the potential to optimize treatment strategies and improve survival outcomes in gastroesophageal cancers.

papers.abstract_en: Advances in spatial omics are shifting the study of lung macrophages from the characterization of isolated transcriptional states toward an understanding of their function in the context of cellular origin, anatomical location, neighboring cells, and tissue architecture. Here, we distinguish the macrophage niche in the strict sense-the local microenvironment that sustains tissue-resident macrophage survival and identity-from the broader cellular niche, in which macrophages are spatially organized with multiple interacting cell populations, and integrate recent insights into lung repair and chronic remodeling. Following injury, remodeling of the resident macrophage compartment, recruitment of monocyte-derived macrophages, and the emergence of regenerative epithelial intermediates and stromal responses generate transient multicellular environments that normally resolve as tissue homeostasis is restored. Spatial analyses, however, indicate that in at least some lung diseases, these repair-associated states fail to resolve and instead become organized into pathological cellular niches characterized by recurrent proximity among aberrant epithelial cells, inflammatory and profibrotic macrophages, activated stromal cells, and extracellular matrix. We further propose a spatial framework in which shared immune-epithelial-stromal interactions can give rise to distinct fibrotic architectures depending on whether they are anchored within alveolar-interstitial regions or around small airways. Finally, we discuss how pathological cellular niches identified by spatial approaches can be functionally validated and translated into therapeutically actionable intercellular circuits.

papers.abstract_en: Miliary intrapulmonary carcinomatosis (MIPC) is a rare metastatic pattern of lung cancer that closely mimics disseminated tuberculosis (TB), posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We present a 53-year-old Filipino woman, a lifelong nonsmoker with prior latent TB, who presented with progressive cough and a diffuse bilateral miliary nodular pattern on chest imaging. An extensive infectious workup was unrevealing, and bronchoscopic biopsy revealed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (TTF-1+) harboring an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. Staging demonstrated brain, osseous, and pleural metastases (stage IVB NSCLC). The patient was initiated on osimertinib 80 mg daily with palliative radiation and zoledronic acid, achieving no evidence of active disease at 2.5 years on serial PET-CT and brain MRI. This case underscores the importance of tissue diagnosis in unresolved miliary patterns, early molecular profiling in lung adenocarcinoma, and the potential for durable exceptional responses with osimertinib in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) continues to present therapeutic challenges because of pathway redundancy and treatment resistance, underscoring the need for multi-target and systems-level strategies. Baicalein (BA), a flavonoid metabolite from Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, shows antitumor potential, yet integrative and immune-related evaluations of BA in LUAD remain limited. METHODS: We integrated network analyses with TCGA-LUAD transcriptomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), network topology, GO/KEGG enrichment, bulk RNA-seq-based immune-infiltration estimation (CIBERSORT), molecular docking, and clinical association analysis (GEPIA2/HPA). Cell viability was assessed in A549 cells​ using the CCK-8 assay, and AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression were further examined experimentally by western blot analysis. RESULTS: A total of 117 candidate BA-LUAD overlapping targets were identified, and six candidate hub genes (EGFR, AKT1, TP53, BCL2, HIF1A, and ESR1) were prioritized. Enrichment analyses suggested that the candidate network was associated with oncogenic signaling and stress-response programs, particularly PI3K-AKT/MAPK signaling, ROS-related processes, apoptosis, and p53 signaling. CCK-8 assays showed that BA reduced A549 cell viability in vitro, with IC50 values of 54.93 μM at 24 h and 22.83 μM at 48 h. Among the prioritized candidates, AKT1 and BCL2 were selected for focused experimental assessment in A549 cells. BA treatment reduced AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression in A549 cells, whereas total AKT1 remained largely unchanged. HIF1A expression showed broad associations with computationally estimated immune-cell fractions and poorer overall survival. CONCLUSION: These findings prioritize a BA-associated candidate network in LUAD involving kinase signaling, apoptosis-related regulation, oxidative-stress responses, and immune-microenvironment associations. The CCK-8 results support an inhibitory effect of BA on A549 cell viability in vitro, and the observed changes in AKT1 phosphorylation and BCL2 protein expression provide focused experimental support for selected components of the candidate network; further in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate biological relevance and translational potential.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Primary pericardial mesothelioma (PPM) is an exceedingly rare, highly invasive cardiac neoplasm with insidious onset and non-specific clinical symptoms. Due to the lack of typical early manifestations and effective routine diagnostic methods, PPM is often misdiagnosed and missed, resulting in delayed treatment and poor prognosis. On admission, he had tachycardia, distant heart sounds, bilateral lower extremity edema, and a 3×2 cm hard, fixed left supraclavicular lymph node. Imaging confirmed pericardial effusion with abnormal pericardial lesions. Ultrasound-guided pericardiocentesis yielded only a small amount of red jelly-like material, with cytology suggesting epithelioid neoplastic cells. Supraclavicular lymph node biopsy confirmed metastatic malignant mesothelioma. Nivolumab immunotherapy showed no improvement. Pericardial tumor resection revealed diffuse, fish-flesh-like tumor invading the myocardium and great vessels. Final pathology confirmed epithelioid-type PPM. CONCLUSION: Patients with recurrent unexplained pericardial effusion and atypical sonographic features, such as flocculent echoes and irregular pericardial thickening, should raise suspicion for PPM. Early recognition of these signs and timely pathological confirmation are critical to avoid diagnostic delays and may improve outcomes.
